user: Felix fell off the monkey bars at school yesterday and broke his wrist. How much can we claim from the Meridian policy?
answer:
DearPolicy

I’m sorry Felix was hurt. For Felix, the policy lists S$600 per accident for a simple (closed) fracture and S$1,500 per accident for a compound (open) fracture; the fracture type must be certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner and confirmed by X-ray, and only one of these benefits is payable for the same bone in the same accident.

A FACT THAT CHANGES THIS ASSESSMENT
Has a registered medical practitioner certified the wrist fracture in writing and confirmed it by X-ray?
This changes what your policy pays under: “Items D and E: the type of fracture must be certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner and confirmed by X-ray. Only one of Item D or” (page 1); “4.4 For Items D and E, a Compound fracture means a fracture in which the broken bone breaks through the skin. All” (page 2)
Answer

user: I was in hospital after that car accident in March. They admitted me at 9:40pm on 14 March and I was discharged at 8:20am on 18 March. How much hospital cash should Meridian pay me?
answer:
DearPolicy

For Simon, Meridian’s “Hospital daily allowance” is S$120 per day, up to 60 days per policy year (page 1), and the policy counts each complete 24 hours as one day and a remaining period of 12 hours or more as another (page 2).

Based on the admission and discharge times you gave, the indicative estimate is S$360; this is not a confirmed payment, and Meridian will require supporting claim documents, assuming at least 3 of the 60 days are still available this policy year.

NEXT STEP

Submit the hospital discharge summary or bill showing the admission and discharge dates and times, together with the policy claim form.

SOURCES
Indicative estimates are worked out from your documents and what you have told me; they are not a payout, and the insurer decides what it pays.

user: Oh, by the way, if one of the kids gets dengue, which of our policies would actually pay anything?
answer:
DearPolicy

For Isla, JuniorShield Child Hospital Income Plan lists “Hand, foot & mouth disease or dengue fever hospitalisation (lump sum)” of S$500; the certificate says it covers illness and accident, but refers to full policy conditions for definitions and exclusions, which aren’t in the document extract I can see.

For Felix, the SafeStay Family Hospital Cash & Personal Accident Plan is accident-only and says confinement due to illness or disease is not covered, so it would not pay for dengue; its child hospital daily allowance is a set amount per day in the schedule, but an endorsement revises it to a set amount per day from 1 July 2026, and the endorsement’s effective date is not confirmed in the records.

For Isla, SafeStay is also accident-only and excludes illness or disease confinement, so it would not pay for dengue.

I couldn’t confirm one of the figures against the cited page of your documents.
